idea: RESHAPE: institutional SMID research sold to funds
buyer: PMs and heads of research at small funds and family offices (£50m-2bn)
pain: No dedicated SMID coverage; a junior analyst costs £60-80k loaded and cannot cover the ground
v1: Two full initiations a month plus model access, delivered as PDF + spreadsheet
channel: Direct to 30-50 named analysts and PMs from her own career, extended by her husband's hedge fund contacts
verdict: Strong, no gate. Same work and same output as the Substack, different buyer and 60x the price. Clears £200k in year one only if contracts are annual and billed upfront.

why.distribution: The buyer is her actual network: 20-50 named warm buyers she can message this week, with peer credibility rather than vendor status, plus a credible route to the rest through her husband's sell-side and hedge fund contacts.
why.demand: Same as the retail version - the pain is well-founded and budgets for research exist, but nothing has been tested with a real buyer and no price has been put in front of anyone.
why.fmf: Exactly the job she did for eight years, sold to the buyer she was. The PM recognises her as one of them, which is the difference between a vendor call and a peer conversation.
why.revenue_structure: Contracted annual retainer, renewal the default once coverage is embedded in a fund's process.
why.defensibility: Relationships, reputation, and an accumulating body of coverage on names nobody else follows. Copyable but not quickly, and the client relationships are sticky.
why.leverage: One note serves every client, but institutional clients ask questions and want calls - bespoke work creeps in and delivery time does not fall to zero.
why.capital: Data (~£10k/yr at the upper end), a domain, a PDF template. Well under £2k to start, and the data spend can wait for the first client.
why.time_to_revenue: She can sell a pilot to a PM she already knows within weeks; realistically 1-3 months to a first signed contract.
why.tailwind: Adverse, and this is the finding worth arguing with. FCA PS24/9 and PS25/4 restored joint research/execution payments, so sell-side SMID coverage may partially recover and research money can flow through commissions again - to firms that execute. She has no execution arm, so she must be paid cash from P&L, the harder sell, precisely as the easy route reopens for brokers.
why.ceiling: £14.4k/yr x 15 funds = £216k gross, less ~£10k data = £206k net. Fifteen clients is a number she can name today.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,200/month per fund = £14.4k/yr. 15 funds = £216k gross, less ~£10k of data = £206k net - clears the bar. BUT only if contracts are annual and billed upfront, which is standard in institutional research and entirely within her control. Sold monthly, the ramp halves year-one cash to ~£130k (signing ~2 funds/month from month 2 gives 22 clients by month 12 and a £317k exit run-rate but only ~£130k collected), making it a year-two business. Decide the billing model before the first conversation.
carries: The buyer is her actual network, the price is 60x the retail version, the sale is a peer conversation rather than a vendor pitch, and the product is identical to the thing she is already good at.
kills: Nothing structural, but the tailwind is genuinely adverse - re-bundling channels research spend back to brokers with execution. Fifteen institutional clients is also a lot of selling for a part-time solo founder.
test: Same test as the retail version: 25 named PMs and analysts, priced proposition, two weeks, £0. This test discriminates between the two variants, which is why it is the only test worth running first.
test_pass: Three or more want the first note and at least one takes it to a budget holder or agrees to a paid pilot.
test_fail: No budget conversation from anyone - the institutional path is not there, leaving only the retail path and its £75k ceiling.
reshape: Explore a small-broker partnership so coverage can be paid via bundled commission rather than cash from P&L - would neutralise the regulatory headwind that is currently the binding constraint.
flags: Publishing free research while later running a fund on the same names needs a personal-account-dealing and disclosure policy designed in from the start.
